candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite one or more fractional parts as equivalent fractions with matching denominators before subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe the same core operation of making fractional parts comparable via common denominators and equivalent fractions. B's version also includes rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator, which A and C place under normalization, so the canonical definition keeps only the shared denominator-equalization concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number or mixed number into a subtraction-ready form, such as converting an improper mixed number to standard mixed form or expressing a whole number as a whole plus zero fractional part.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A and C explicitly combine whole-number rewriting and improper mixed-number normalization into one setup skill. B narrows the label to mixed-number normalization, but its exclusions show the same boundary with alignment and borrowing. This is the closest cross-expert match, with B representing a slightly narrower version of the same preparation concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract once quantities are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators of like fractions and subtracting whole-number and fractional parts of mixed numbers without borrowing.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: The three experts use nearly identical names and definitions for the direct subtraction step after setup is complete. Minor wording differences about combining results do not change the underlying concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Borrow across whole and fractional parts when needed during subtraction, then simplify and express the result in lowest terms, integer form, fraction form, or mixed-number form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts combine post-subtraction regrouping/borrowing with simplification and final expression of the answer. Names differ slightly, but the cognitive concept and boundaries are the same.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks are highly consistent and align into four shared skill concepts with full 3/3 consensus. The main variation is boundary placement between denominator alignment and normalization: Expert B includes rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator under alignment, while Experts A and C place that under normalization. Otherwise, the codebooks show near one-to-one correspondence across all skills, and every skill_id maps cleanly to exactly one candidate concept.
